name: n8n Cloud
tagline: Workflow automation platform with self-hosted and cloud options

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked; public 2026 references list Starter around €20 annual-effective / about $24 monthly depending billing and currency.
pricing.freeTier: No free cloud plan, just a trial; self-hosting the open source core is free.

tiers.name: Community Edition (self-hosted)
tiers.limits: Unlimited workflows, steps and users in the software; hosting, database and operations are user-supplied.
tiers.notes: Free self-hosted software, not a free n8n Cloud tier.

tiers.name: Starter (Cloud)
tiers.limits: 2,500 executions/month, 1 project, 5 concurrent executions, 2,300 AI credits/month, 7-day logs and 2.5 GB stored execution data.
tiers.notes: Vendor price is €24 monthly or €20/month billed annually; converted at ECB 2026-08-10 EUR/USD 1.1555.

tiers.name: Pro (Cloud)
tiers.limits: 10,000 executions/month, 3 projects, 20 concurrent executions, up to 13,700 AI credits/month, 30-day logs and 25 GB stored execution data.
tiers.notes: Vendor price is €60 monthly or €50/month billed annually; converted at ECB 2026-08-10 EUR/USD 1.1555.

tiers.name: Business (self-hosted)
tiers.limits: 40,000 executions/month, 6 projects and 30-day insights; self-hosting required.
tiers.notes: Vendor annual price is €667/month equivalent; converted at ECB 2026-08-10. A monthly commitment exists, but its current public price was not exposed.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom executions, unlimited projects, 200+ concurrency and up to 365-day insights.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free n8n Cloud plan; Community Edition is free to self-host with unlimited workflows/users, but infrastructure is not included
pricing.billingTerms: Starter/Pro monthly + annual; Business published annual price; 14-day Business trial and no-card Starter/Pro trial; VAT/tax may apply
pricing.hiddenCosts: An execution is one complete workflow run regardless of steps. AI credits reset and expire monthly, cannot be carried over or purchased separately. Business overage is €4,000 (about $4,622.00) per additional 300,000 executions; no prorated refunds.

verdictSummary: Because n8n itself is open source, the core cloud subscription can be replaced by self-hosting if you can own hosting, updates, and backups.
coreLoopDIY: Self-host n8n, connect credentials, create workflows, and run a small VPS with backups.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay to avoid maintaining an automation server that their business workflows depend on.

priorArt.name: n8n
priorArt.desc: The product's open-source workflow automation core.

alternatives.name: Activepieces Community Edition
alternatives.desc: A genuinely open-source workflow runner with a simpler one-container path.

facts.install: Run one Docker container for personal/testing use, or Docker Compose with PostgreSQL and Redis for production.
facts.engines: AI pieces connect to providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google Gemini using user-supplied credentials.
facts.dataFormat: Single-container mode stores data under ~/.activepieces; production uses PostgreSQL and Redis, with files/logs optionally in S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Activepieces has a smaller node ecosystem and requires you to provide the uptime, upgrades, backups and security n8n Cloud manages.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Docker; public webhooks need a reachable HTTPS URL, while production also needs PostgreSQL, Redis and managed secrets.

alternatives.name: Automatisch
alternatives.desc: A smaller AGPL automation server for people who do not need n8n's entire ecosystem.

facts.install: Clone the repository and run Docker Compose.
facts.dataFormat: Application and credential data stays on the user's server in PostgreSQL, with Redis for queues/cache; credentials are encrypted.
facts.gapVsPaid: Automatisch is much narrower than n8n's ecosystem and still leaves every operational responsibility with you.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Docker, PostgreSQL/Redis configuration and secret management; the default sample login must be changed immediately.

alternatives.name: n8n Community Edition
alternatives.desc: The same workflow engine without the cloud bill; you inherit updates, backups, and uptime.

facts.install: Install with Docker or npm; Docker is the recommended production path.
facts.engines: AI nodes connect to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama and many other model/vector backends.
facts.dataFormat: SQLite stores workflows, credentials and executions by default; PostgreSQL is supported, with binary data in the database, filesystem or object storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: It is the same core workflow engine, but the cloud plan's managed upgrades, backups, availability and support all disappear.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a server, HTTPS and a public webhook URL for many integrations, plus ongoing updates, backups and provider credentials.

notes: A perfect page for 'yes, but hosting/ops becomes your job'.
prompt:
Build me a self-hosted n8n setup to replace n8n Cloud. Requirements:

- Do not rebuild the tool, n8n is open source. Set it up properly on my VPS instead.
- Docker Compose: the official n8n image with SQLite storage (fine at personal
  scale, skip Postgres), a named volume for /home/node/.n8n, restart
  unless-stopped.
- n8n binds to 127.0.0.1 only, published through my existing reverse proxy on an
  HTTPS subdomain; n8n's own user management guards the editor.
- Set N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY explicitly in .env and tell me to back that key up
  separately. Losing it orphans every stored credential, say so loudly.
- Webhook env vars (WEBHOOK_URL) set to the public subdomain so external services
  can call my workflows.
- Nightly backup script: export workflows and credentials with n8n's CLI plus copy
  the data volume to backups/YYYY-MM-DD/, keep 14 days.
- An update script that pins a version tag, backs up first, then pulls and
  restarts. Never run :latest blind.
- Import two starter workflows as JSON smoke tests: an RSS-to-email digest and a
  webhook-to-Telegram alert.
- Out of scope: multi-user teams and high-availability scaling. This is one
  person's automation box.
- README: first-boot owner account, a backup restore drill, and the update
  routine. Ops is the subscription being replaced here.
